questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CKAD skills: wiring ConfigMaps and Secrets, configuring InitContainers, implementing TLS sidecars, setting up readiness/liveness probes, and crafting a NetworkPolicy with conditional egress.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-driven feature flags
- Secrets for credential management
- InitContainers for tooling installation
- TLS sidecars for secure communication
- Readiness and liveness probe configuration
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-config
data:
  ENABLE_API: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  token: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: app-namespace
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-policy
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: internal-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: curlimages/curl:latest
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'echo Initialized']
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: ENABLE_API
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: feature-config
                  key: ENABLE_API
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: api-creds
                  key: token
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
        - name: tls-sidecar
          image: nginx:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 443
```

## Trade-offs
- **NetworkPolicy complexity**: The policy above allows egress only to the internal-api pod. A more permissive approach might allow DNS resolution but restrict target services.
- **InitContainer overhead**: Installing curl in every pod increases startup time and image size. Consider baking tools into the base image if startup latency is critical.
- **Sidecar maintenance**: A TLS sidecar adds complexity and resource overhead. For simple use cases, TLS could be handled within the application container directly.
- **Secret security**: Storing credentials in a Secret is fine for basic scenarios, but consider external secrets operators or vault integration for production environments requiring rotation.
- **Probe configuration**: Aggressive probe settings can cause unnecessary restarts; conservative settings may delay failure detection. Tune based on application startup time.

Why This Is Asked

Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: static-content-server
  namespace: ckad-demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: static-content
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: static-content
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: html
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: static-content-pvc
        - name: template
          configMap:
            name: page-template
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: page-config
      initContainers:
        - name: init
          image: alpine
          command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /template/index.html /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html"]
```

```yaml
kind: ServiceAccount

  name: orch-sa
  namespace: ops
---
# Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: orch-pod-access
  namespace: ops
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]

- apiGroups: [""]

apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: orch-binding
  namespace: ops
subjects:

  name: orch-sa

  kind: Role
  name: orch-pod-access
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to safely patch CronJobs, leverage InitContainers for bootstrapping from ConfigMaps, enforce security context non-root, and apply sensible history limits. It also probes operational testing and rollback strategy for scheduled jobs.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob controls: concurrencyPolicy, history limits, startingDeadlineSeconds
- InitContainers and ConfigMaps for bootstrapping
- PodSecurityContext: runAsNonRoot
- Probes on Jobs' pods and resource requests/limits
- Testing and rollback of scheduled jobs

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CronJob patch outline (conceptual)
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: nightly
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: backup-sa
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
          initContainers:
            - name: init-backup
              image: busybox
              command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /config/backup.sh /backup/backup.sh"]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backup-config
                  mountPath: /config
                - name: backups
                  mountPath: /backup
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: backup-tool:latest
              resources:
                requests:
                  memory: "128Mi"
                  cpu: "100m"
                limits:
                  memory: "256Mi"
                  cpu: "500m"
              readinessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /livez
                  port: 8080
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /readyz
                  port: 8080
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backups
                  mountPath: /backups
          volumes:
            - name: backups
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: backups-pvc
            - name: backup-config
              configMap:
                name: backup-config
```

## Why This Is Asked
Assess ability to constrain scheduling to hardware and perform safe rolling updates for GPU workloads.

## Key Concepts
- NodeSelector and taints/tolerations
- GPU resource requests/limits
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- RollingUpdate strategy and preStop
- Verification and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ai-processor
  namespace: ml
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ai-processor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ai-processor
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        hardware: gpu
      tolerations:
      - key: hardware
        operator: Equal
        value: gpu
        effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
      - name: ai-processor
        image: your-image:tag
        resources:
          requests:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            memory: "2Gi"
            cpu: "500m"
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            memory: "4Gi"
            cpu: "1000m"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /live
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1
      maxSurge: 1
```

## Verification Under Load
1. Deploy and verify pods schedule on GPU nodes: `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide`
2. Check GPU allocation: `kubectl describe nodes | grep nvidia.com/gpu`
3. Load test with concurrent requests while monitoring pod health
4. Verify rolling updates maintain availability: `kubectl rollout status deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
5. Monitor GPU utilization during load: `nvidia-smi` on target nodes

## Rollback Strategy
1. Use deployment revision history: `kubectl rollout history deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
2. Quick rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
3. For critical issues, scale to zero then redeploy previous stable version
4. Monitor rollback progress and verify pod health and GPU allocation

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical RBAC auditing skills within the CKAD scope, including multi-namespace governance, secure logging, and egress constraints.

## Key Concepts

- **RBAC objects**: RoleBindings, ClusterRoleBindings, and ServiceAccounts at the namespace level
- **ConfigMap-driven policy**: External policy reference for audit rules
- **Namespace-scoped auditing**: Decentralized audit model vs. cluster-wide approaches
- **Pod lifecycle**: InitContainers for tool installation, readiness/liveness probes for reliability
- **Storage**: PVC-backed logging at /logs
- **Network security**: Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting egress to the audit endpoint

## Trade-offs

- **Pros**: Decentralized scaling, namespace isolation, ConfigMap flexibility for policy updates
- **Cons**: Resource overhead per namespace, potential for policy drift, Secret management complexity, duplicated effort across namespaces

## Minimal YAML Skeleton

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: rbac-policy
data:
  policy.yaml: |-
    allowedBindings:
      - kind: User
        name: admin
    maxServiceAccounts: 10
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  bearer-token: <token>
  endpoint: https://audit.example.com/api/v1/digest
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rbac-auditor
  namespace: target-ns
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rbac-auditor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rbac-auditor
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: busybox
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - "wget -qO /tools/curl https://curl.se/download && wget -qO /tools/jq https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7.1/jq-linux64 && chmod +x /tools/*"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
      containers:
        - name: auditor
          image: alpine:latest
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              apk add --no-cache curl jq
              while true; do
                kubectl get rolebindings,clusterrolebindings,serviceaccounts -o json > /logs/snapshot.json
                curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @/logs/snapshot.json $ENDPOINT
                sleep 3600
              done
          env:
            - name: TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: audit-credentials
                  key: bearer-token
            - name: ENDPOINT
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: audit-credentials
                  key: endpoint
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: audit-logs
        - name: tools
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: target-ns
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rbac-auditor
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: audit-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
```

## Why This Is Asked

Static-site serving in a per-namespace context tests PVC/ConfigMap/Secret integration, nginx config via ConfigMap, and safe multi-tenant limits with quotas and limits.

## Key Concepts

- Deployments, replicas, and rolling updates
- PVCs for shared data, ConfigMaps for content and nginx.conf, Secrets for credentials
- nginx basic auth integration via config map
- ClusterIP Service exposure and Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace ResourceQuota and LimitRange for multi-tenant safety

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal skeleton showing core resources
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: site-content
data:
  index.html: |-
    <html>...</html>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nginx-config
data:
  nginx.conf: |
    server { listen 80; location / { auth_basic "Restricted"; auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/.htpasswd; root /usr/share/nginx/html; } }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: basic-auth
type: Opaque
data:
  # base64(encoded username:password)
  htpasswd: <base64>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: static-site
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:stable
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        volumeMounts:
        - name: site
          mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
          subPath: nginx.conf
        - name: auth
          mountPath: /etc/nginx/.htpasswd
          subPath: htpasswd
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: site
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: static-site-pvc
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: nginx-config
      - name: auth
        secret:
          secretName: basic-auth
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: static-site-svc
spec:
  selector:
    app: static-site
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
    protocol: TCP
  type: ClusterIP
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: static-site-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
```

- How would you update content without downtime?
- How would you rotate credentials and reflect it in nginx without redeploying pods?

Why This Is Asked

Gives candidates a concrete task focusing on PodSecurity basics, not just data pipelines. It combines ConfigMap/Secret usage, a simple audit logic, and a secure, isolated network path.

## Key Concepts

- Deployment scope per namespace
- InitContainer installation of tooling
- ConfigMap-driven rules
- Secret-based credentials
- HTTP POST of results
- TLS cert rotation sidecar
- NetworkPolicy egress scoping
- Readiness/liveness probes

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: namespace-security-audit
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: namespace-security-audit
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: namespace-security-audit
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq yq && echo ready"]
      containers:
        - name: audit-agent

          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: audit-portal-credentials
      volumes:
        - name: audit-scripts
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: audit-pvc
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

Tests CKAD fundamentals in a practical way: probes, resources, and ConfigMap usage. It checks that the candidate can translate requirements into Kubernetes primitives and reason about reliability.

## Key Concepts
- Liveness vs readiness probes

- ConfigMaps as configuration and env binding
- Volume mounts and envFrom/KeyRefs

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web-app
        image: registry.example.com/web-app:v1.2
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          timeoutSeconds: 3
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 256Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 512Mi
        env:
        - name: APP_MODE
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: web-app-config
              key: APP_MODE
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /etc/config
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: web-app-config
```

## Key Concepts

- ConfigMap vs Secret usage
- envFrom vs volumeMounts
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- RollingUpdate strategy
- Resource requests/limits

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-config
data:
  APP_PORT: 8080
  LOG_LEVEL: info

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: app-secrets
stringData:
  DB_PASSWORD: mypassword

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api
    spec:

        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:

        - secretRef:

        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15

            memory: 128Mi
```
